title: Ordinary regular parameters in a free logarithmic chart
statement: Let $(X,M,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth], with triviality locus $U\subseteq X$. Let $e:W\to X$ be an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] with $W$ affine and locally Noetherian, and suppose the inverse-image log structure on $W$ admits a chart $\mathbf N^r\to M|_W$, for $r\ge0$. Write $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ for its structural functions and $f=\prod_{i=1}^r t_i$. Then the inverse-image log structure is log regular, $W$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], and $e^{-1}(U)=D(f)$. For every $w\in W$ and geometric point $\bar w$ above it [def-weil-geometric-point], put $B=\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $A=B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and $J=\{i:t_i\notin B^\times\}$. The characteristic monoid at $\bar w$ is canonically $\mathbf N^J$; the ideal of images of nonunits of the log stalk in $A$ is $(t_j:j\in J)A$. The indexed list $(t_j)_{j\in J}$ extends to a regular system of parameters both in $A$ and in $B$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. In particular the ordinary-local assertion concerns the given functions on the actual etale chart. If $J$ is empty, $f$ is a unit in $B$; the empty product is $1$.

proof.text: Apply etale_logRegular_restriction to obtain fine saturation, log regularity of N and equality of its triviality locus with the inverse-image locus.
At every geometric point apply freeLogChart_strict_parameters to obtain the monomial-normalized characteristic isomorphism, transported ideal equality and the strict-coordinate parameter extension.

Apply strictLocal_parameters_descent to the list obtained by mapping the actual coordinate function over nonunitIndices. List.map_map identifies the lists in its hypothesis and conclusion with the strict and ordinary parameter lists of this theorem.

For each ordinary point choose the geometric point from an algebraic closure of its residue field. The ordinary list extension generates the maximal ideal with dim entries; spanFinrank <= number of distinct entries <= length proves regularity. Therefore W is a regular scheme.

Use the characteristic isomorphism to prove that the characteristic is subsingleton exactly when every coordinate is a unit. If a nonunit index existed, the constant zero and constant one functions on J would contradict subsingletonness; conversely an empty J makes the function monoid subsingleton. An algebraic-closure point detects the converse at each ordinary point. A ring homomorphism preserves finite products, and a finite product is a unit iff each factor is a unit. Scheme.mem_basicOpen_top now identifies the locus with the indicated basic open. The same product calculation proves the unit implication; r=0 gives an empty product equal to 1.
